subject: Dressing-room storage that feels calm
hook: No spare room? You can still have a dressing room feel.
fb:
One we hear a lot: "I'd love a dressing room, but we haven't got a spare room."

Honestly, you don't need one. Most of what makes a dressing room feel calm is the planning, not the floor space — internal drawers, a proper shoe section, one finish from end to end, and a fixed place for everything behind closed doors.

A single wall of fitted wardrobes in the main bedroom can do most of that. If you've got an alcove or a run under the window, a slim dressing table can finish it off.

Got a question about your own room? Ask away in the comments, or book a free, no-obligation consultation below.

Do you need a whole spare room to get a dressing room? No — and it's one of the most common questions we're asked.

Most of what makes a dressing room feel calm comes from planning rather than floor space. A full wall of fitted wardrobes in your main bedroom can include internal drawers, a dedicated shoe section, long and short hanging, and dividers for accessories, all behind closed doors in one consistent finish. Add a slim dressing table under a window or in an alcove and you have most of the experience without giving up a room.
